pie: owis eḱwoi kʷe
english: The Sheep and the Horses

pie: tód ḱeḱluwṓs h₂ówis Héǵrom bʰugét.
english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the plain.

pie: mógʰew ḱléwse h₁eǵóh₂ h₁idʰé pékʷtōr. h₂éHsh₂m̥ h₂usési h₂réydʰe. puHróm ph₂wéni stnéh₂mi h₁ím-kʷe gʷʰr̥néwmi. péh₂urih₁ pékʷeti pékʷtōr bʰéwdʰeti. h₁yós ne bʰéwdʰeti só h₁ím h₁éwseti. h₁éy suHrós? h₁yód h₁éy suHrós h₁éseti h₁éy ne h₁wésus. h₁yód h₁éy swéh₂deti wiḱpóteyey h₁ím bʰoréye. h₁yód séh₂eti nu h₁ddʰí.
english: Listen, boy: I am the cook here. At dawn prepare the hearth. I set the wheat on the fire and heat it. The fire cooks; the cook stays awake. The cook who is not awake, he burns it. Is it sour? If it is sour, it is not good. When it has become tasty, carry it to the master. When he is sated, then eat.

pie: h₁yód h₂wést h₂nḗr h₁éǵʰs gʷéh₂t. ugʷsénn̥s yéwgt h₂roh₁dʰéyet-kʷe. méh₂ter dʰéǵʰom séh₁mn̥ h₁áyso h₁íd-kʷe h₂éle. n̥sméy polh₁ú ǵr̥h₂nóm dh₃dʰí gʷr̥néHomes-kʷe te. h₂érh₃trom h₂éǵrom térdt séh₁mn̥-kʷe h₁ím séngʷt. h₁ésyo pótnih₂ séngʷʰet.
english: When it grew bright, the man went out. He yoked the oxen and spoke: "Mother Earth, receive the seed and nourish it. Give us much grain, and we will praise you." The plough split the field, and the seed fell into it. His wife sang.

pie: dʰúgh₂ter moḱs sth₂dʰí nókʷts linékʷti. h₂éHsh₂m̥ gʷh₂dʰí péh₂wr̥-kʷe spéḱye. h₁yód h₂éydʰos néḱeti h₂susyóntn̥s h₃ósdons bʰére. h₁íns h₁ésyeh₂i logʰéye h₂éydʰōy-kʷe pnéwmn̥ dh₃dʰí. nu Hwérdʰt h₃ósdons léyǵʰti dʰégʷʰeti-kʷe. péh₂wr̥ ḱóymom gʷʰr̥néwti kʷsépm̥-kʷe h₂epó h₂éǵeti. péh₂wr̥ nókʷtm̥ pér ph₂sdʰí. ń̥h₂eydʰos ḱóymos stéwdt.
english: Daughter, rise early; the night is leaving. Go to the hearth and look at the fire. If the fire has gone out, bring dry twigs. Lay them on it and give the fire breath. Then it grows strong; it licks the twigs and burns. Fire warms the house and drives away the night. Guard the fire through the night. A fireless house grows cold.

pie: sh₂wéns kʷékʷlos wértetor h₃épos-kʷe nos h₁íh₁ ḱóm wértetor. h₁yód dʰéǵʰōm tinéh₁eti h₂érh₃ye. h₁yód gʷʰéreti séh₁ye. h₁yód ǵr̥h₂nóm pékʷētor h₂éḱesi skinddʰí. h₁yód ǵʰéyōm gʷémeti h₂Hséh₂i sddʰí h₁ddʰí-kʷe. nu h₂érh₃trom h₃roǵéye séh₁mn̥-kʷe ph₂sdʰí. ḱód h₁léwdʰerosyo wiHrósyo wérǵom.
english: The wheel of the sun turns, and our work turns with it. When the earth thaws, plough. When it grows warm, sow. When the grain has ripened, cut off the ears. When winter comes, sit down at the hearth and eat. Then straighten the plough and guard the seed. This is the work of a free man.

pie: h₂ówis h₁éḱwōskʷe
english: The Sheep and the Horses

pie: déywoǵenh₁es ḱéh₂ ph₂wéns wékʷesh₂ ḱludʰí. wódr̥ ph₂wéni mē Hyéh₁ks. péh₂wr̥ sóh₂wl̥-kʷe próti mē h₃méyǵʰes. h₁n̥gʷnís deywós. dʰéh₁leh₂ nos dedórḱe. h₁ím h₂susyóntyeh₂h₁ péwḱeh₂h₁ h₂éle h₂léksēti-kʷe te. péh₂wr̥ nékʷti stége h₂usési bʰéwdʰt.
english: Of-Divine-Race, hear these words about the fire. Do not throw water on the fire. Do not urinate toward the fire or toward the sun. Agni is a god. He sees our deeds. Feed him with dry pine, and he will protect you. At night cover the fire; at dawn it wakes.

pie: h₁ést mógʰus h₁yós wérǵom ne lubʰyét. h₁yód wiḱpótis h₂érh₃yet ń̥werǵos pr̥kʷéwi Hn̥dʰí légʰyet. h₁yód h₂éḱesh₂ skinédt ń̥werǵos ḱéyo. gʷémt ǵʰéyōm. ǵr̥h₂nóm h₁ésyo ḱóymoy ḱéyo. ń̥werǵos kénket. wiḱpótim gʷémt h₂isḱét-kʷe kʷid. wiḱpótis wérh₁t h₁yós ne h₂érh₃yeti só kénketi.
english: There was a servant who did not love work. When the master ploughed, the idle one lay under the oak. When he cut the ears, the idle one lay still. Winter came. Grain lay in his house. The idle one was hungry. He came to the master and sought something. The master said: "He who does not plough, he is hungry."

pie: nókʷts gʷegʷóme péh₂wr̥-kʷe dʰégʷʰeti. méh₂ter ǵénh₁mn̥h₂ h₁ésmi logʰéyeti. h₁íh₂ h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂h₁ stégeti kh₂néti-kʷe. ǵénh₁mn̥h₂ l̥gʰté ḱwṓ wos h₂lékseti. ph₂tḗr wos h₂ew gʷegʷóme h₁éḱwōs stesth₂ḗr. dʰoHnéh₂ h₁n̥dóm ḱéyor ne kʷis kénketi. wĺ̥kʷos h₂én h₁ésti. nu kh₂nét h₁íh₂-kʷe swopéyet.
english: Night has come, and the fire burns. The mother lays the children down by it. She covers them with wool and sings: "Lie down, children; the dog guards you. Your father has come back; the horses are standing still. The grain lies inside; no one is hungry. The wolf is yonder." So she sang, and she put them to sleep.

pie: h₁yód gʰóstis h₁éreti h₁ím péh₂wr̥ wédʰe. h₁ím ph₂wéni sodéye h₁ésmey-kʷe dʰoHnéh₂m dh₃dʰí. h₁yód h₂éḱh₃eti nu h₁ésyo h₁nómn̥ mléwHeti. gʰóstis deywóybʰos priHós. h₁yós gʰóstim h₂epó h₂éǵeti deywṓs tóm gʷʰnénti. h₁ésmey h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m logʰéye légʰeti-kʷe. h₁yód léyteti h₁ésmey h₂éh₂usom dh₃dʰí.
english: When a guest arrives, lead him to the fire. Seat him by the fire and give him grain. When he has eaten, then he will tell his name. The guest is dear to the gods. Whoever drives a guest away, the gods strike him down. Lay wool for him, and let him lie down. When he goes away, give him gold.

pie: sporéh₂m h₂erh₃tóm moḱs bʰére. h₁íd pér stéygʰe sporéh₂m-kʷe Hih₁kdʰí. h₁íh₂m̥ stége. h₁yód sporéh₂ h₁ésmi h₁épi légʰēti ǵʰwḗres wórmeyes-kʷe h₁íh₂m̥ gʷr̥h₃ónti. h₁yód h₂wérseti séh₁ye. wódr̥ séh₁mn̥ h₂életi sóh₂wl̥-kʷe ǵr̥h₂nóm pékʷeti. h₁yóti séh₁mn̥h₂ séh₁yēsi tóti h₂éḱesh₂ bʰuHyéti. séh₁mn̥ gʰrémonth₁ ḱr̥déh₁ mē Hyéh₁ks. nu gʷṓs h₂epó h₂éǵe.
english: Carry the seed to the ploughed land early. Walk through it and cast the seed. Cover it. If the seed lies on it, the wild beasts and the worms devour it. When it has rained, sow. Water nourishes the seed, and the sun ripens the grain. As many seeds as you sow, so many ears grow. Do not cast seed with an angry heart. Then drive the cattle away.

pie: wiHrṓs swóm wérǵom r̥h₁dʰént. kʷékʷlōs h₂éḱesh₂ ḱléytreh₂m wéǵʰont. h₁suh₁éḱweh₂ pótnih₂ ḱléytreh₂m puHróh₁ pl̥néh₁t. pékʷtōr h₁ím h₂réydʰet gʷr̥h₃ónt-kʷe. píph₃ont gʷéHyont-kʷe deywóns-kʷe gʷr̥nHént. déywōs h₁uséwōm déh₃tores n̥sméy ǵr̥h₂nóm h₂ew dh₃té. gʰósteyes pékʷtorm̥ gʷr̥nHént.
english: The men accomplished their work. The wagons carried the ears to the shelter. Good-Horses, the mistress, filled the shelter with wheat. The cook prepared it, and they ate. They drank and sang and praised the gods: "Gods, givers of good things, give us grain again!" The guests praised the cook.

pie: h₁yód h₂néres h₂éḱesh₂ h₁n̥dóm wéǵʰōnti h₁íh₂ sh₂wéni logʰéye h₁íh₂-kʷe h₂sowséyeti. h₁yód h₂wérseti h₁íh₂ ḱléytreh₂m sl̥h₂gʷdʰí. kʷíd h₁íh₂ h₂sowséyomes? tinh₁ónt ǵr̥h₂nóm suHróm bʰúHt. nu h₁íh₂ h₁n̥dóm dʰh₁dʰí. nu ǵr̥h₂nóm ǵʰyémi h₁ésti ǵénh₁mn̥h₂-kʷe ne kénketi.
english: When the men bring the ears in, lay them in the sun, and it dries them. If it rains, take them to the shelter. Why do we dry them? Grain that grows moist becomes sour. Then put them inside. So in winter there is grain, and the children are not hungry.

pie: pérkʷunos upér gʰrémet. h₁éḱwōs troméyont pṓlHōs-kʷe l̥gʰént. h₂énh₁mos h₂éḱesh₂ Hrunépt. h₁wesuḱléwēs h₁éǵʰs gʷéh₂t h₂éǵrom-kʷe widétām. bʰéyh₂t ǵr̥h₂nóm néḱt. nu h₁ésyo pótnih₂ sokʷéyet mē bʰéyh₂s. puHrós n̥sméy h₁n̥dóm h₁ésti. h₂ew séh₁yōmes ǵr̥h₂nóm-kʷe bʰuHyḗti.
english: Perkwunos roared above. The horses trembled and the foals lay down. The wind broke the ears of grain. Of-Goodly-Fame went out and saw the field. He grew afraid; the grain was lost. Then his wife said: "Do not be afraid. We have wheat inside. We will sow again, and the grain will grow."

pie: h₂éǵros h₂susyét séh₁mn̥-kʷe ne bʰuHyét. gʷówes tr̥syónt ḱwónes-kʷe légʰyont. h₁suḱléwēs wiḱpótis dyḗm spéḱyet h₂roh₁dʰéyet-kʷe. dyéw ph₂ter n̥sméy wódr̥ dh₃dʰí. nékʷti h₂wérst. dʰéǵʰōm moḱs tinéh₁t séh₁mn̥-kʷe h₂wékst. gʷówes ḱwónes-kʷe píph₃ont. h₁suḱléwēs méwdt ph₂térm̥-kʷe dyḗm gʷr̥néHt.
english: The field was dry, and the seed did not grow. The cattle were thirsty, and the dogs lay down. Good-Fame, the master of the house, looked at the sky and spoke: "Father Sky, give us water!" In the night it rained. Early the earth grew moist, and the seed grew. The cattle and the dogs drank. Good-Fame rejoiced and praised Father Sky.

pie: príHe séh₁mn̥ ǵr̥h₂nósyo ph₂tḗr. h₂erh₃tóm h₁ésyo méh₂tēr. dyḗws h₁íd gʷʰr̥néwti h₁íd-kʷe h₂életi. h₁yós h₂érh₃yeti só-kʷe h₂éǵrosyo poh₂imḗn. séh₁mn̥ h₂éǵrom-kʷe ph₂sdʰí. h₁yós ḱód wóyde só h₃péwst. téwe-kʷe ḱóymos ǵr̥h₂nóh₁ pl̥nh₁ih₁tó.
english: Friend, the seed is the father of the grain. Ploughed land is its mother. The sky warms it and feeds it. And the man who ploughs is the shepherd of the field. Guard the seed and the field. He who knows this grows rich. And may your house be filled with grain.

pie: dʰúgh₂ter gʷówes HrudHénti. h₁éǵʰs gʷh₂dʰí h₁íns-kʷe h₂ml̥ǵdʰí. h₁éymos séngʷʰe sth₂éh₁yonti-kʷe. trésonts kʷid só ne dédeh₃ti. nu h₁íns h₂éǵrom h₂éǵe ḱwṓ-kʷe h₁íns péh₂sti. h₁yód h₁regʷesyḗti wĺ̥kʷos gʷm̥sḱéti. nu gʷṓs ḱléytreh₂m h₂ew wédʰe. pṓlHos swéh₂m méh₂term̥ ḱléytreh₂i sékʷetor.
english: Daughter, the cows are lowing. Go out and milk them. Sing to them, and they stand still. The one that trembles with fear gives nothing. Then drive them to the pasture, and the dog guards them. When it grows dark, the wolf comes. Then lead the cows back to the shelter. In the shelter the foal follows its mother.

pie: h₁yód dʰúgh₂ter téwe wiHróm gʷéh₂esi h₁ésyo méh₂term̥ stérge. h₁ésyo swésorm̥ bʰréh₂term̥-kʷe lubʰyé. h₁ésyo péh₂wr̥ ph₂sdʰí. moḱs sth₂dʰí wérǵom-kʷe wr̥ǵdʰí. h₁yéh₂ bʰéwdʰeti séh₂ pótnih₂ ḱóymom h₁usúbʰis pl̥néh₁ti. h₁ésyeh₂s-kʷe h₁nómn̥ ḱlutóm. ḱéh₂ wékʷesh₂ memn̥dʰí.
english: Daughter, when you go to your husband, cherish his mother. Love his sister and his brother. Guard his fire. Rise early and do the work. A wife who is wakeful fills the house with good things. And her name is famous. Remember these words.

pie: príHe ḱwṓ h₂éǵroy téwe bʰréh₂tēr. h₁ím h₂éle. h₁yód légʰyēsi h₂ówins h₂lékseti. h₂ḱh₂owsyéti kʷsépi ḱlush₁yéti. h₁yód wĺ̥kʷos gʷm̥sḱḗti HréwdHti. h₁ím mē stunéds h₁ím ph₂wéns mē h₂éǵes. h₁yód leléykʷeti wĺ̥kʷos h₁íh₂n̥s gʷr̥h₃éti.
english: Friend, the dog is your brother in the pasture. Feed him. When you lie down, he guards the sheep. He hears well; he hears at night. When the wolf comes, he cries out. Do not strike him; do not drive him from the fire. If he is gone, the wolf devours them.

pie: bʰréh₂ter h₂éydʰos ne dʰégʷʰeti h₃ósdons bʰére. kúdʰe h₁éyes h₁sénti? ḱléytreh₂i ḱéyror. bʰréh₂tēr h₁íns wéǵʰet h₁íns-kʷe ph₂wéni logʰéyet. h₂éydʰos Hwérdʰt swésōr-kʷe dʰoHnéh₂m gʷʰr̥néwt. kénkesi bʰréh₂ter? kénkoh₂. nu sddʰí h₁ddʰí-kʷe. h₂éydʰoy-kʷe sdtā́m dʰoHnéh₂m-kʷe h₂ḱh₃tā́m.
english: "Brother, the fire is not burning; bring branches." "Where are they?" "They lie by the shelter." The brother brought them and laid them on the fire. The fire grew strong, and the sister heated grain. "Are you hungry, brother?" "I am hungry." "Then sit down and eat." And the two sat down by the fire and ate up the grain.

pie: sóh₂wl̥ puHróm h₂éǵroy pékʷet. h₂éḱesh₂ pléh₁dʰet. wiHrṓs moḱs h₁éǵʰs gʷh₂ént. h₁íh₂ skindént h₁íh₂-kʷe h₁n̥dóm wéǵʰont. pótnih₂es ǵr̥h₂nóm h₂sowséyont. gʷéHyont. wiHrṓs swidyónt dʰugh₂téres-kʷe tóybʰos wódr̥ bʰéront. h₁yód h₁regʷesyét wiḱpótis tóybʰos misdʰóm déh₃t. nu h₁édn̥t sh₂ént-kʷe.
english: The sun ripened the wheat in the field. The ears swelled. Early the men went out. They cut them off and brought them inside. The wives dried the grain. They sang. The men sweated, and the daughters brought them water. When it grew dark, the master gave them their wage. Then they ate and were sated.

pie: h₁suh₁éḱweh₂ pótnih₂ bʰéwdʰt mogʰúbʰos-kʷe h₂roh₁dʰéyet. túH h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m tn̥nudʰí. túH ph₂wéney h₃ósdons bʰinddʰí. túH-kʷe h₂ówins h₂éǵrom h₁l̥h₂dʰí. túH kʷékʷlom h₂réydʰe. h₁eǵóh₂ pékʷoh₂. h₁éǵʰs gʷh₂ént wérǵom-kʷe wr̥ǵént. h₁yód h₁ludʰónt h₁suh₁éḱweh₂ tóybʰos ǵr̥h₂nóm déh₃t.
english: Good-Horses, the mistress, awoke and spoke to the servants: "You, stretch out the wool. You, split branches for the fire. And you, drive the sheep to the pasture. You, make the wagon ready. I cook." They went out and did the work. When they arrived, Good-Horses gave them grain.

pie: swṓy yéwgesey h₁nómn̥h₂ dʰh₁dʰí. h₁yós h₁nómn̥ wóyde só te ḱlush₁yéti. h₁yód tóh₁ yéwgesi tóysōm h₁nómn̥h₂ h₂roh₁dʰéye. h₁yód pérkʷum h₁ludʰḗtes tóh₁ h₂ew wodʰéye. tóybʰos mē gʰrémes. tóybʰos séngʷʰe h₂érh₃trom-kʷe duktés.
english: Set names on your team. One that knows its name listens to you. When you yoke them, speak their names. When they arrive at the oak, lead them back. Do not rage at them. Sing to them, and they pull the plough.

pie: deywóḱlewēs wérǵōy h₃rēǵés h₂éǵroy wérǵt. h₂érh₃trom déwkt séh₁mn̥ Hyéh₁kt h₂éḱesh₂ skinédt. h₁yód ǵr̥h₂nóm h₁n̥dóm h₁ést h₃rḗǵs h₁ésmey misdʰóm puHrósyo méh₁tim déh₃t. deywóḱlewēs swéh₂ey méh₂trey h₁ím bʰoréyet. h₁ím widét méwdt-kʷe. sokʷéyet méne súHnew h₁wésu wérǵom wérǵs. téwe ḱléwos ń̥dʰgʷʰitom h₁syéh₁t.
english: Fame-from-the-Gods did the work in the king's field. He drew the plough, he cast the seed, he cut off the ears. When the grain was inside, the king gave him a wage, a measure of wheat. Fame-from-the-Gods carried it to his own mother. She saw him and rejoiced. She said: "My son, you have done good work. May your fame be imperishable."

pie: dʰúgh₂ter wódr̥ h₁n̥dóm bʰére. dʰoHnéh₂m h₁ésmi dʰh₁dʰí h₁íd-kʷe ph₂wéni stn̥h₂dʰí. h₁yód h₁íd yésēti dʰoHnéh₂ pékʷetor. h₁yód h₁íh₂ h₁éwsētor téwe ph₂tḗr gʰrémeti. h₂éHsh₂m̥ mē linékʷs sísde bʰéwdʰe. h₁yód h₁íh₂ swéh₂deti h₂nr̥bʰós h₁íh₂m̥ h₁opéye. kénkontes tr̥syóntes-kʷe tóy h₂éǵrōd gʷm̥sḱónti. h₁yós h₂éḱh₃t só wr̥ǵyéti.
english: Daughter, bring water inside. Put the grain in it and set it on the fire. When it boils, the grain cooks. If it burns, your father grows angry. Do not leave the hearth; sit and watch. When it has become tasty, give it to the men. They come hungry and thirsty from the field. He who has eaten, he works.

pie: príHe me ḱludʰí kéh₂ilom mē h₂éḱh₃s. sh₁méney h₁wésu ǵr̥h₂nóm dʰh₁dʰí. h₁íd wr̥míbʰos ḱéle. h₁yós séh₁mn̥ h₁ḗdti só ne séh₁yeti. séh₁mn̥ ḱóymōy h₂éh₂usom. ḱód memn̥dʰí téwe-kʷe ǵénh₁mn̥h₂ gʷíh₃woyh₁t.
english: Hear me, friend: do not eat up the whole. Set aside the good grain for seed. Hide it from the worms. He who eats the seed, he does not sow. Seed is gold to the household. Remember this, and may your children live.

pie: h₁yód déywoǵenh₁es ǵr̥h₂nóm pékʷēsi h₁n̥gʷnéyey kʷid dh₃dʰí. h₁n̥gʷnís h₁uséwōm déh₃tōr. n̥smé gʷʰr̥néwti n̥smé-kʷe h₂életi. h₁ésmey ḱéywōys wékʷesbʰis h₂roh₁dʰéye. h₁ń̥gʷney ḱā́m h₂éHsh₂m̥ h₂lékse n̥sméy-kʷe h₁suménēs h₁syéh₁s. méne moy méh₂tēr ḱéh₂ wéwket.
english: Of-Divine-Race, when you cook grain, give some to Agni. Agni is the giver of good things. He warms us and feeds us. Speak to him with dear words: "Agni, guard this hearth, and may you be kindly to us." My mother told me these things.
